Azerbaijan Recalls 2018 Currency Crisis and Its Aftermath

BAKU — Six years after Azerbaijan’s 2018 manat crisis rattled the economy, officials and residents alike are reflecting on the challenges the country faced and the lessons learned in recovering from the financial turmoil.

The crisis began in February 2018, when a sudden drop in global oil prices triggered a sharp devaluation of the Azerbaijani manat. Within weeks, the currency lost nearly 35% of its value against the US dollar, sparking panic among businesses and ordinary citizens. Prices of imported goods surged, and many families saw their savings evaporate almost overnight.

“The most difficult period was the spring of 2018,” recalled Nigar Aliyeva, an economist at the Caspian Economic Center. “Inflation soared to 19% by April, and people rushed to convert their savings into dollars.” The government was forced to intervene, imposing temporary restrictions on currency exchanges and raising interest rates to stabilize the manat.

Azerbaijan’s Central Bank governor at the time, Samir Suleymanov, defended the emergency measures. “Our priority was to prevent further depreciation and restore confidence in the financial system,” he said in a recent interview. “We understand the hardships people faced, but these actions were necessary.”

Small businesses were particularly hard-hit. According to the Union of Regional Entrepreneurs, nearly 4,500 small firms closed or suspended operations in the first half of 2018. “It was a nightmare for traders,” said Elchin Mammadov, who owns a food import business in Ganja. “We had to change prices almost daily.”

Despite the initial shock, economic activity gradually recovered by late 2019 as global oil prices rebounded and government support programs took effect. Today, officials say Azerbaijan’s economy is stable, with inflation under 4% and the manat holding steady.

“The 2018 crisis taught us the importance of strong financial reserves and diversification,” said Finance Minister Lala Imamalieva. “We are better prepared for future challenges.”
